name: Alchemist
summary: A Universal World Class any character may take regardless of their class. It levels through the bench: dissolving, calcining and bottling at first, then distilling, filtering and reacting, then subliming and the Great Work of transmutation. Past level 3 the levels never stop, and each one grants two perks: potency, duration, quality, yield or containment.
_namespace_note: This is the alchemist WORLD CLASS (rules.worldclass.get / rules.alchemist), not the PF1e Alchemist character class in content/classes/ (rules.classes.get). They share a name and nothing else: a Rogue is an Alchemist here the way a Fighter is an Herbalist, by doing the work. The two namespaces never meet in code.
_ruling_2026_10_05_note: The owner's alchemy revamp rulings (docs/alchemy-questions.md, all ten rounds, and the plan's open points answered 2026-10-06; docs/alchemy-revamp-plan.md §4, §7). Three unlock levels replace five: level 1 dissolve, calcine, bottle and assay on common and uncommon material; level 2 distill, filter and react on rare and exotic; level 3 sublime and transmute on legendary. Seal became Bottle; Precipitate folded into Filter (the precipitate is Filter's solid end); Stabilize became an ingredient (any material with the `stabilizer` working trait); Catalyze became a working trait (`catalyst`, never spent). The old level 4 and 5 rows, the 25/65/50/100 curve and the `legendary-work` milestone and its deed are removed. Old saves keep their level: an old Alchemist 4 or 5 is an endless level 4 or 5 with its perk picks banked (the `alchemy_v2` migration, wave 2 lane I).
_thresholds_note: Mastery to reach levels 2 and 3, herbalism's and the forge's numbers kept equal on purpose ('the two tracks are meant to pace the same', plan §4.1); every level after that is priced by `endless`. The bench pays each successful step (1, +1 per rarity band above common, +1 at Superior, +2 at Flawless or higher; every success pays, the owner's 2026-10-05 ruling), and firsts pay 3.
_endless_note: Plan §4.2: two picks a level, the same perk twice allowed, stored on Progress.perks and read live. Potency +5% to the benefits of everything made, duration +10%, quality +1 to the ceiling, yield +5% chance per Bottle of one more unit (the engine rolls it and shows the roll), containment -1 DC a pick on a volatile step and each mishap's dice one step smaller (1d6, 1d4, 1d3, 1; never below 1 point). All proposed numbers, tunable here.
_ceiling_note: `ceiling` is the highest quality index a level's hands reach (0 Crude, 1 Sound, 2 Fine, 3 Superior, 4 Flawless): Fine, Superior, Flawless at 1 to 3 (plan §4.3), each Quality perk one step more.

tools: alchemist's field kit: a crucible, a spirit lamp, a rack of vials, a funnel and cloth
levels.note: Roadside work: dissolving in a jar, burning to a calx, bottling the result, and assaying a pinch of what you carry. The four classics are known from the start.
Distilling (in a laboratory), filtering the drawbacks out of a solution, and the reaction that is the dangerous heart of the craft. Rare and exotic material, which needs a laboratory.
The slow furnace and the Great Work: subliming a solid to its crystal, and turning a material into a rarer one of its kind. Both in a laboratory.

method_descriptions.dissolve: Takes solids up into a solvent: a solution, which pours and can be bottled, reacted or filtered.
method_descriptions.calcine: Roasts a solid in the crucible to its calx. A combustible material burns away instead; it does not calcine.
method_descriptions.bottle: Pours the work into its vessel and stoppers it. The vessel decides what the product is: a vial is drunk or poured on, a clay flask thrown, a casing struck, a rod lit. Matches a known formula, or experiments.
method_descriptions.assay: Tests a pinch of a reagent against a drop on a glass slide: one benefit and one drawback learned. Volatile and toxic reagents make it dangerous.
method_descriptions.distill: Runs a liquid through the alembic and keeps the hearts of the run: two measures make one spirit, half again as strong. Needs a laboratory.
method_descriptions.filter: Passes a solution through cloth: every drawback stays on the cloth as a precipitate, and the filtrate runs clean at nine tenths of its strength.
method_descriptions.react: Sets two or more inputs against each other in a liquid medium, drop by drop: their traits merge, and the same trait from two materials adds its grades.
method_descriptions.sublime: Heats a solid in the aludel and scrapes the crystal crust that forms above: two measures make one sublimate, half again as strong. Needs a laboratory.
method_descriptions.transmute: The Great Work: two of a material (one, with a catalyst that names it) become one of a rarer material of the same kind that shares an essence. A day in progress. Needs a laboratory.

_method_help_note: `method_help` is what the bench shows beside the button: what the method DOES, what it NEEDS to be legal, and what a player reaches FOR it to accomplish.

dissolve.does: Makes a solution carrying every trait of what went in, same-named traits adding their grades up to your level.
dissolve.needs: A solid and one solvent (water, spirits, vinegar, oil or acid).
dissolve.for: Starting almost every line: a solution can be bottled, reacted or filtered.

calcine.does: Makes a calx (a salt) that keeps indefinitely and carries the solid's traits.
calcine.needs: A solid that does not burn away.
calcine.for: A powder you can bottle or sublime, and a way to keep a reagent that would spoil.

bottle.does: Makes the finished product. A formula's core takes one slot; the rest are your picks. Drawbacks of what you used come along unless filtered.
bottle.needs: A liquid or a powder, and a vessel. Bottling always comes last: a finished product is never an input.
bottle.for: Every product: potions, oils, splash flasks, clouds and tools.

assay.does: Reveals one benefit and one drawback of a reagent, and pays 1 mastery for each.
assay.needs: A pinch of the reagent: a tenth of one you carry.
assay.for: Knowing what a reagent does before you build with it.

distill.does: Two measures of a liquid make one spirit at x1.5 potency and duration, one rarity band rarer. Each concentration step is harder.
distill.for: Concentrating a solution or a solvent into something stronger than any one reagent.

filter.does: Strips every drawback; the filtrate keeps its benefits at x0.9, and the drawbacks stay on the cloth as a precipitate.
filter.needs: A solution, a spirit or an admixture.
filter.for: Antitoxin, antiplague, and any line where a reagent's cost must not reach the bottle.

react.does: Merges the inputs into an admixture; same-named traits add their grades, capped by your level.
react.needs: Two or more inputs, one of them a liquid medium.
react.for: Building a trait up to a higher grade, and mixing reagents that would not go into one solution.

sublime.does: Two measures of a solid make one sublimate at x1.5 potency and duration, one rarity band rarer.
sublime.for: Concentrating a salt or a calx.

transmute.does: Two of a material (one, with philosopher's mercury) become one of the same kind, one band rarer, sharing an essence. You choose which.
transmute.needs: A laboratory, and a day: the work waits In progress until you collect it.
transmute.for: The rare reagent the market does not sell.

_bench_note: Every number the plan marks proposed, as rule rows (plan §7, §8, §9, §12; contracts §8). `order` is the method strip. Per method: `where` (kit or lab), `bulk` (every method batches, plan §15.2), `minutes` per unit of world time, `takes`/`makes` in words, `form` (the intermediate it makes), `per_unit` (inputs one unit consumes: Distill and Sublime take two measures for one, plan §7.2) and `tuning` (the minigame's numbers the check response carries; bands start generous, both earlier sweeps found every crafting minigame was softened after launch). `in_progress_after` is plan §12.3's threshold: a step longer than this waits In progress, with the clock moved only by its `hands_on` minutes. `lab_rank`: rare and above need a laboratory (plan §14). `lab_bonus` is the book's alchemist's lab, +2 circumstance (UE p.77). `lab_rate_cp_per_hour` is the fallback rent until lane G's `market.lab_rent` lands (plan §14, 2 sp an hour, proposed).

calcine.name: Calcine
calcine.takes: a solid that does not burn away

filter.name: Filter
filter.takes: a solution, a spirit or an admixture
filter.makes: a filtrate, and a precipitate of what it held back

react.name: React
react.takes: two or more inputs, one a liquid medium

bottle.name: Bottle
bottle.takes: a liquid or a powder, and a vessel
bottle.makes: the finished product; the vessel decides which kind

transmute.name: Transmute

transmute.makes: one of a rarer material of the same kind

bench._slots_note: Plan §6.3 (proposed, Atelier's three and the Physick flask's two): what a finished product carries in benefits. A formula's core takes one. Intermediates carry everything in the pool up to `intermediate`; the player picks when there is more.
bench._routes_note: Plan §5.3, §12.1: the routes a family delivers a benefit through (`benefit`), and the routes on which a drawback reaches whoever uses it (`drawback`). A trait on any other route is shown dimmed with the reason and dropped, never silently kept. A tool carries only its function: light and smoke (`tool_types`).
bench._family_note: How each family is used and what it keeps (plan §12.1). `how` is the use door's words (rules/consumables.py: drink, apply, throw, coat, light); `action` the book's; `keeps` minutes before it goes off (null: indefinitely). The book's potions do not spoil.
bench._forms_note: The intermediates (plan §6.3, §12.1): what each method makes, whether it pours, and how long it keeps (solutions and admixtures 3 days, spirits a year, salts indefinitely). Sellable; a finished product is never an input.
bench._traits_note: Working traits at the bench (plan §5.5). `band` scales the minigame's window (a catalyst or apparatus widens it 20%; slow to dissolve narrows Dissolve's 30%); `roll_twice` is Pathfinder Unchained's pure material, the check rolled twice and the better kept, as the forge reads it.
bench._transmute_note: Plan §9 (proposed): DC 10 + 5 a band above common for the output (uncommon 15, rare 20, exotic 25, legendary 30); a catalyst whose job names Transmute (philosopher's mercury) makes it one for one.
bench._catalyst_jobs_note: The named jobs of catalysts that are never spent (plan §5.8; lane D's drafts in docs/alchemy-review.md). A catalyst set in the catalyst role is never spent and puts no trait in the pool; set as an ordinary input it is spent and its traits pool like any reagent's (a unicorn horn shaving's two). Built: one_for_one (Transmute), strip_one (a drawback, as Filter does), stabilizes (a stabilizer that is not spent), roll_twice (pure). Orichalcum's 'names the formula' is not built.
bench._protection_note: What spares the alchemist a `toxic_to_handle` reagent (plan §8.4): a laboratory's fume hood, or a mask and gloves carried. The goods row is lane H's; until it lands the pack is read by these names, the way the forge found its field kit.
bench._kit_note: The alchemist's field kit (plan §14): common and uncommon work anywhere. Lane G's `places.has_alchemy_kit` decides when it lands; until then the kit folds out wherever the character stands, as the forge's did before lane G.

_old_methods_note: What a removed method became (plan §4.1, Q3.1), for an old recipe or chain naming it.
